column1: # Atomicity guard exemption list — internal/core/guards/atomicity_guard_test.go
# (TestAtomicityGuard_UnclassifiedMultiWriteFunction) fails the build when a
# non-test function on *KeyorixCore/*AnomalyDetector makes 2+ storage/core
# writes outside a WithTransaction closure and has no entry here. Seeded from
# Session O's O1 triage (~/proj/prompts/reports/SESSION-O.md) — every hit from
# the coordinator's txscan (32) plus the blind-spot core-to-core sweep (6) was
# individually read and classified before being listed.
# Rows whose function field starts with "AUDIT:" instead belong to
# TestAtomicityGuard_AuditBeforeWrite (Session O follow-up, 2026-09-29,
# scratch/txscan2): a SUCCESS audit event that textually precedes a later
# storage write in the same function. Kept as a distinct key namespace (not
# a plain function-name row) because the SAME function can legitimately need
# both a write-count exemption above AND an audit-before-write exemption
# here, for unrelated reasons (see handleSessionReuse/RevokeLease, which have
# both). There is no equivalent for TestAtomicityGuard_TransactionEscape
# (ESCAPE) — that check is never exemptable; see its own doc comment.
# Columns: function <TAB> class <TAB> reason
# Classes:
#   B — consume-first by design: a single-use value is consumed BEFORE later
#       work and must stay consumed even if later work fails (replay
#       protection). See the function's own `// atomicity: consume-first by
#       design` comment and its verifying test (Session O, O4).
#   C — independent steps by design: partial completion is safe and
#       self-healing (a later run/retry naturally corrects it).
#   D — false positive: the flagged calls are on MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches
#       (if/else, switch) — never actually sequential — or the function is
#       already atomic via a single storage primitive with the flagged calls
#       being deliberate best-effort follow-ups.
#   S — saga (compensating-action): no single DB transaction is available
#       (the writes span audited, individually-locked core choke points like
#       AssignUserRole/RemoveUserRole, not raw storage calls), so the function
#       instead tracks what succeeded and reverts it on a later failure, with
#       the revert's own failure audited loudly. Reviewed and accepted as this
#       codebase's established alternative to a DB transaction for this shape
#       (see TransitionMembership's revertFailedActivation, the original
#       reference instance).
#   TEMP-A — a genuine, confirmed class-A atomicity bug (must be fixed, not
#       exempted) with an OPEN, NOT-YET-MERGED fix PR already up. Listed here
#       ONLY so this guard can be merged without immediately breaking CI on
#       unfixed main — remove the line as part of merging the cited PR (the
#       fix wraps the writes in WithTransaction, so the function naturally
#       stops being flagged once merged; the TSV line becomes dead weight, not
#       actively wrong, if left — but should be cleaned up).
# Rows whose function field starts with "JIT:" are a third key namespace, for a
# function that needs a SECOND, independent classification because two
# unrelated groups of writes inside it were reviewed separately. The namespace
# exists for the same reason "AUDIT:" does, and is NOT optional: both readers
# key a plain row on the function name alone and keep the LAST one, so a second
# plain row for an already-listed function would silently RECLASSIFY it --
# which, for a class-B function, would break the oracle exemption that rests on
# that class (server/faultops TestConsumeFirstExemptions_MatchAtomicityLedger
# requires B). A "JIT:" row documents without shadowing. Both readers now also
# refuse a duplicate key outright, so this cannot be got wrong silently.
# Rows whose function field starts with "CONSUME:" are a fourth key namespace,
# for the same reason: the single-use-value spend inside a function whose plain
# row has a different class (e.g. a class-S saga). The consume-first oracle
# exemption (server/faultops consume_first_oracle_test.go) reads the CONSUME:
# row, so it rests on exactly that claim and not on the saga row.
# Never add a class-A (real, unfixed, no-open-PR) entry here. Fix it instead.
(*KeyorixCore).bootstrapSystemLocked
column3: #2295 merged 2026-09-29: the real bootstrap path now runs entirely inside one WithTransaction (tx.* calls, correctly invisible to this scan), with LogUserCreated/LogProjectCreated audited only after commit. The 2 remaining c.storage calls this guard sees are on MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches: SetSystemMetadata (the "total > 0" backfill case for a pre-fix install, which returns immediately after) and AddPasswordHistory (the post-commit best-effort seed in the actual first-boot path) -- the backfill branch never reaches the password-history line. Re-verify this class if #2246 (still open at review time; adds its own audit-ordering changes on top of #2295) touches this function's control flow.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).PurgeExpiredComplianceRecords
column3: Per-type purge batches, independently `rec()`'d, self-healing next scheduled run.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).FinishWebAuthnLoginPending
column3: MFA challenge + WebAuthn session consumed before mintSession; trailing UpsertMFAStepupToken/CreateMFAStepUpGrant are best-effort UX convenience post-mint. Verified fail-closed: TestFinishWebAuthnLogin_MintFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed (Session O, O4, PR #2310). #2693 review (2026-11-21, REVIEW-4543-DEEP-1): the mint call is now mintLoginSession (webauthn.go), for this row and the passwordless row below.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).FinishWebAuthnPasswordlessLoginPending
column3: Same shape as FinishWebAuthnLoginPending. Verified: TestFinishWebAuthnPasswordlessLogin_MintFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed (Session O, O4, PR #2310).

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RefreshSession
column3: The 2 DeleteSession calls are on mutually exclusive early-return branches (ceiling exceeded / account inactive); RotateSession is already one atomic CAS transaction (#211).

column1: (*KeyorixCore).VerifyMFACredentials
column3: Challenge consumed first; TOTP vs recovery-code are mutually exclusive attempts. Verified: TestVerifyMFALogin_MintFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed exercises this via its caller VerifyMFALogin (Session O, O4, PR #2310). #2693 review (2026-11-20): No longer flagged: the TOTP and recovery-code consumes moved into lowercase helpers (markTOTPStepUsedAfterMatch, consumeRecoveryCodeRecovering; #3277, #3557), so only ConsumeMFAChallenge is counted. Kept because server/faultops TestConsumeFirst_NonExemptOpStillFailsTheOracle (login_fault_classes_test.go) and the oracle_a_by_design consumedBy rows require class B here. Since #2567 a matched TOTP step is released when the session mint returns an error (not after a panic, #3277); the challenge, and a recovery code if one was used, stay consumed.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).verifyMFAStepUpCode
column3: TOTP attempt then recovery-code attempt, consume-shaped. Verified: TestVerifyMFAStepUp_GrantFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed (Session O, O4, PR #2310). #2693 review (2026-11-20): No longer flagged (same helpers, #3277/#3557), and TOTP vs recovery code is now an exclusive if/else on the code's shape. Kept for the consume-first oracle's class-B cross-check.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RevokeLease
column3: The 2 UpdateDynamicSecretLease calls are on mutually exclusive branches (engine.Revoke fails -> revoke_failed; succeeds -> revoked). #2693 review (2026-11-20): The write is now RecordDynamicSecretLeaseRevocation (renamed by #2698); still one call per exclusive branch.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).refreshCertNotAfterCache
column3: The 2 SetSecretCertNotAfter calls are on mutually exclusive branches (cert parses / doesn't).

column1: (*KeyorixCore).requireReauth
column3: MarkTOTPStepUsed / ConsumeMFAStepUpGrant are alternative verification paths, consume-shaped. Verified: existing TestRequireReauth_GrantConsumedOnFirstAction_SecondDifferentActionRejected and siblings (mfa_stepup_grant_single_use_test.go); re-confirmed in scope during Session O, O4, PR #2310. Scope note (ORACLE-A-1, 2026-10-05): consumes NOTHING when called from ActivateMFA -- activation runs with user.MFAEnabled still false, so secondFactorEnrolled is false and the bare-password branch is taken. ActivateMFA's own row below covers that path; do not attribute ActivateMFA's burned LastUsedStep to this function. #2693 review (2026-11-20): Correction: the ActivateMFA scope note holds only for an account with no second factor. secondFactorEnrolled is MFAEnabled || WebAuthnEnabled, so a passkey account adding TOTP does consume a reauth step-up grant here before activation; it stays consumed if activation fails (fail-safe). ActivateMFA's doc comment is corrected to match.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).ActivateMFA
column3: Its OWN MarkTOTPStepUsed (internal/core/mfa.go, not requireReauth's -- see that row's scope note) burns the matched enrolment-code time-step BEFORE the activation transaction, and must stay burned if that transaction fails, or a stolen enrolment code is replayable inside its +/-1-step window. Verified: TestActivateMFA_ActivationFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed (consume_first_fails_closed_test.go), red/green-proved -- its red proof folds the consume into the transaction and shows the replay then succeeds. Added by ORACLE-A-1 (2026-10-05) after coordinator review on PR #2840 found the oracle exemption for REST POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/activate citing requireReauth, which does not perform this consumption. Also consumed by server/faultops' consumeFirstExemptions via TestConsumeFirstExemptions_MatchAtomicityLedger, which requires this row to read B.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).handleSessionReuse
column3: DeleteSession (legacy, no-family) / DeleteSessionsByFamily are on mutually exclusive branches. The real gap here was a swallowed single-write error, not multi-write atomicity — fixed by auditing loudly on DeleteSessionsByFamily failure (Session O, O2 item 2, PR #2298); the branch shape itself is unchanged and still textually flagged.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).FinishWebAuthnReauth
column3: ConsumeWebAuthnSession before CreateMFAStepUpGrant; fails closed (grant-creation failure returns an error with the session already consumed and no grant issued). Verified: TestFinishWebAuthnReauth_GrantFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed (Session O, O4, PR #2310) — no prior test existed for this function at all.

column1: (*AnomalyDetector).detectOneSecretAnomalies
column3: Independent per-rule alert saves, failure count aggregated, not fatal.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).applyNewPassword
column3: Password hash + account-state ARE already correctly transactional. The 2 flagged writes are the best-effort tail: AddPasswordHistory (reuse-policy only, self-healing) and RevokeAllPersonalAccessTokensForUser (security-relevant; its failure is now audited loudly rather than silently swallowed — Session O, O2 item 2, PR #2298). #2693 review (2026-11-20): The flagged pair is now AddPasswordHistory + PrunePasswordHistory (besteffort.Run). The PAT revocation moved into revokePATsAfterPasswordChange and is audited loudly on failure.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RotateSecretOnDemand
column3: switch on the upstream backend-rotation result — mutually exclusive branches; already has an explicit partial-state audit trail (ROTATION-001).

column1: (*KeyorixCore).bulkDeleteOneSecret
column3: Per-item body of BulkDeleteSecrets' loop (extracted so a panic on one item can be recovered without losing earlier items' results); each item's fetch+delete is independent, failures collected in the result rather than aborting the batch — correct design for a bulk operation. #2693 review (2026-11-20): Reclassified C -> D: the only counted writes, DeleteSecret and DeleteSecretWithPermissionCheck, are on the actorID == 0 if/else, so at most one runs per call. The independent-items property above belongs to BulkDeleteSecrets' loop.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).RevokeUserCredentialsForDeactivation
column3: Reclassified from the coordinator's preliminary "A": verified ValidateSessionToken/ValidatePATToken BOTH independently re-check IsActive/AccountLoginBlocked on every use, cold path and the warm-cache path, so a failed revocation here leaves only an inert row, never a live credential — self-healing, not a real gap. See SESSION-O.md's O1 table for the full verification. #2693 review (2026-11-20): Correction: until #4537 the warm-cache PAT path re-checked only the token row, not the owner, so a failed RevokeAllPersonalAccessTokensForUser left the PAT usable from the auth cache for up to validTokenTTL. Since #4537 CurrentPATRestriction reads the owner in the same statement on every cache hit, so the claim holds for every credential type.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).CompleteSAML
column3: ConsumeSSOLoginState (single-use login state, replay protection) is consumed before mintSession; the trailing RecordLogin is an explicitly-commented best-effort last-login stamp. Fails closed by construction: a mintSession failure returns an error with the login state already consumed. New finding — a mixed storage-write + core-to-core-write shape invisible to a scanner that only counts one call style at a time (this guard's own historical txscan/corescan split would each have seen only 1 write here, not 2+).

column1: JIT:(*KeyorixCore).CompleteSAML
column3: Andrei's decision on #2839 item 1 (2026-10-09): the JIT-provisioning and group/role-reconciliation writes are class C -- independent, self-healing steps -- a SEPARATE classification from the class-B row above, which by its own stated reason covers only the ConsumeSSOLoginState consumption and deliberately does not stretch to User/UserGroup/UserRole. Self-healing because provisionSSOUser and reconcileSSOGroups/reconcileSSORoles are each idempotent and converge on the next successful login, and because a half-applied run leaves a USABLE account rather than a corrupt one: nothing is half-written, the account simply has not logged in yet. Accepted WITH three conditions, each enforced by a test that is red when broken, in internal/core/saml_jit_class_c_test.go -- (1) mintSession runs only if provisionSSOUser AND both reconciles fully succeeded; any error means no session (TestCompleteSAML_GroupReconcileReadFailureRefusesTheLogin, _FailedGroupRemovalRefusesTheLogin, _RoleReconcileReadFailureRefusesTheLogin, with _CleanReconcileStillMintsASession as the calibration that stops the condition being met by refusing everything); (2) reconcile removes as well as adds and derives roles only from the validated assertion (_ReconcileRemovesAsWellAsAdds, _RolesDerivedOnlyFromTheValidatedAssertion); (3) JIT account creation is audited even when the login then fails (_JITProvisionIsAuditedEvenWhenTheLoginThenFails). Condition 1 did NOT hold before this row: both reconcile calls returned nothing and swallowed every error, so a failed REVOCATION -- the IdP drops a user from its admin group and the removal errors or is refused -- left the privilege in place and still minted a session. Fixed in the same PR; class C is only sound WITH that fix, since the sole protection against a half-applied reconcile is refusing to mint a session over it. SCOPE: the reconcile claims (conditions 1 and 2, and 1a/2a below) cover BOTH login paths. CompleteSAML, and since #2907 the OIDC login CompleteSSO, which reaches the same reconcileSSOGroups/reconcileSSORoles through syncSSOGroups/syncSSORoles and refuses the login on their error the same way (internal/core/oidc_reconcile_refusal_test.go: TestCompleteSSO_FailedGroupRemovalRefusesTheLogin, _PartialRoleReconcile_TwoOfThreeApplied, _LastAdminGroupRemovalRefused; calibrations _EmptyGroupsClaimReconcilesToZero, _AbsentGroupsClaimLeavesMembershipsAlone). OIDC presence comes from extractTokenStringList's `present`. The JIT-provisioning claims (condition 3) are pinned for CompleteSAML. #2903 review follow-ups, same tests file plus internal/core/saml_reconcile_refusal_test.go (real SQLite, persisted state read back): (1a) every refused reconcile writes exactly one FAILED audit event naming each failed step and the already-applied, not-rolled-back counts -- auth.sso_reconcile_refused, or auth.sso_reconcile_last_admin_removal_refused when the last-admin guard refused a removal (_FailedRemovalWithNothingElseToChangeIsAudited, _ReconcileReadFailureIsAudited, _PartialGroupReconcile_AddAppliedThenRemovalFails, _PartialRoleReconcile_TwoOfThreeApplied, _LastAdminGroupRemovalRefused, _LastAdminRoleRevocationRefused, calibration _AdminGroupRemovalWithASecondAdminSucceeds); (2a) a PRESENT-but-empty groups attribute reconciles to zero, an ABSENT one is a no-op (_EmptyGroupsAttributeReconcilesToZero, _AbsentGroupsAttributeLeavesMembershipsAlone; internal/saml TestExtractAssertion_GroupsPresenceIsDistinctFromEmptiness).

column1: (*KeyorixCore).ReconcileRBACPermissions
column3: Startup top-up reconciliation (ADR-044), explicitly documented as additive/non-clobbering/best-effort in its own doc comment: a failure just means the next server restart retries the same reconcile. New finding via this guard's broader verb coverage. #2693 review (2026-11-20): Correction: before #4542 a failed grant was not retried (the next run saw the permission as existing and returned). Since #4542 each new name is listed in system_metadata before it is created and its grants are retried every startup until all land; since REVIEW-4542-M1 the row (rbac_reconcile_pending_grants_v2) lists each (permission, role) pair, so only the roles whose grant has not landed are retried, and the run holds the rbac-permission-reconcile named lock.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).completeInvitationAccept
column3: CreateUser, then consumeInspectedToken (consume-first), then applyInvitationGrants, then UpdateProjectInvitation -- deliberately ordered (see the function's own extensive comments) with compensating reverts on BOTH failure points: a grants failure soft-deletes the orphaned account (fault-injection-proven recoverable via a resent link, Session O follow-up 2026-09-29, PR #2313 -- the coordinator's own hand-found candidate, confirmed class A at the time and fixed, not S by inspection alone), and the final race-loss path reverts via revokeInvitationGrants (unchanged, pre-existing). Reference-quality saga once fixed. #2693 review (2026-11-20): Wording out of date: there are now four undo points (abandonInvitationAccept after a failed link consume, a failed grant or a failed accept write, plus the race-loss revert), and the race-loss path also removes the account. The saga claim holds.

column1: CONSUME:(*KeyorixCore).completeInvitationAccept
column3: #4410 (INVITE-ACCEPT-NOV-1): the link-spend step of the class-S saga above, classified on its own so the consume-first oracle exemption (server/faultops consume_first_oracle_test.go) rests on exactly this claim and not on the saga row. consumeInspectedToken spends the setup link after CreateUser and before the grants; when a later step fails, abandonInvitationAccept removes the account (with its baseline system_viewer role and password history, removeInvitationAcceptAccount, one transaction) and reverts the grants, but the link stays spent: a consumed token never becomes live again, and the inviter resends, which issues a fresh link for the still-pending invitation. Verified: internal/core TestCompleteInvitationAccept_FailureAtEachStep_UndoesAndSaysWhatHappened, TestCompleteInvitationAccept_PanicAtEachStep_UndoesTheAccept, TestCompleteInvitationAccept_AbandonRemovesBaselineRoleAndPasswordHistory.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).ReconcileAlertsWriteRole
column3: F1 (ADR-110 follow-up, PR #2244) one-time backfill: AssignPermissionToRole is called once per role inside a loop, each iteration independent (a failure just logs and continues to the next role); the completion marker (SetSystemMetadata) is only set after the whole loop, so a role that didn't get granted this run is simply re-attempted on the next startup — the per-role check (`hasAlertsWrite`) already makes re-granting an already-granted role a no-op. Self-healing on retry, matching ReconcileRBACPermissions' own C classification above. seedAlertOperatorRole (called from this same function) had a genuine class-A bug — role creation and its permission grant not wrapped together, so a failure between them permanently stuck the role at zero permissions — fixed in the same PR by wrapping both in one WithTransaction, not exempted here.

column1: AUDIT:(*KeyorixCore).AlertNewAnomalies
column3: Reviewed (Session O follow-up 2026-09-29, coordinator-named "worth a look"): the audit/SIEM event for a detected anomaly fires before MarkAnomalyAlertAlerted; the function's own comment explains that if marking fails, the loop retries this same anomaly on the next scheduled pass, re-emitting the SAME event -- "the audit event is already out, harmless dup". Over-alerting on failure is the safe direction (detection, not access control).

column1: AUDIT:(*KeyorixCore).RevokeLease
column3: False positive from branch-blindness (same root cause as this function's plain write-count D entry above): the flagged writeAuditEventFull@844 ("dynamic_lease.revoke_failed") and the storage.UpdateDynamicSecretLease@852 it's compared against are on MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches (engine.Revoke fails vs succeeds) -- never both reached in one call. #2693 review (2026-11-20): Correction: the cited names and lines are stale (now writeAuditEventFailedFull on the revoke-failed branch and RecordDynamicSecretLeaseRevocation). The success branch also writes dynamic_lease.revoked BEFORE RecordDynamicSecretLeaseRevocation in the same call. Accepted: the target credential is already revoked (engine.Revoke succeeded), the audit result feeds the row's RevokeError, and a failed row write returns an error and is retried.

column1: AUDIT:(*KeyorixCore).bootstrapSystemLocked
column3: LogUserCreated@437 fires only AFTER the bootstrap transaction has already committed (txErr == nil checked first, per #2295/#2246's "Audit only AFTER the transaction has committed" comment) -- the later storage.AddPasswordHistory@449 is unrelated, best-effort post-commit bookkeeping whose failure cannot retroactively make "user created" false. Re-verify if this function's control flow changes. #2693 review (2026-11-21, REVIEW-4543-DEEP-1): line numbers are stale: now auth_bootstrap.go:485 (LogUserCreated) and :492 (AddPasswordHistory, inside besteffort.Run). The reasoning still holds.

column1: AUDIT:(*KeyorixCore).completeInvitationAccept
column3: LogUserCreated@222 fires only after c.CreateUser's OWN internal transaction has already committed -- the user genuinely exists at that point, and stays true regardless of a later applyInvitationGrants/UpdateProjectInvitation failure in THIS function (which now compensates via a soft-delete, PR #2313 -- a distinct, later fact, not an undo of "was created"). #2693 review (2026-11-21, REVIEW-4543-DEEP-1): the line number is stale: LogUserCreated is now setup_consume.go:459, right after the account-create write returns. The reasoning still holds.

column1: AUDIT:(*KeyorixCore).handleSessionReuse
column3: Confirmed real (Session O follow-up 2026-09-29, coordinator-named "worth a look"): EventSessionReuseDetected's original wording ("... -- revoking the session family") asserted an outcome before the revoke was attempted, and could still fail. Fix open: PR #2298 (reworded to state only the detected fact). Remove this line when it merges. #2693 review (2026-11-20): Reclassified TEMP -> D: the cited fix (#2298, dba72a283) merged and the event now states only the detected fact. Not removed, because the audit still textually precedes DeleteSessionsByFamily; a failed family revoke has its own EventSessionReuseFamilyRevokeFailed.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).MarkNotificationRead
column3: PAT-GUARD-1: the 2 calls are on MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches (no PAT restriction -> MarkNotificationRead; restricted PAT -> MarkScopedNotificationRead); each is one UPDATE.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).MarkAllNotificationsRead
column3: PAT-GUARD-1: the 2 calls are on MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches (no PAT restriction -> MarkAllNotificationsRead; restricted PAT -> MarkAllScopedNotificationsRead); each is one UPDATE, so read-all stays all-or-nothing.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).completePasswordSetup
column3: AUTH-2 item 1 (#3298): every write that makes up the consume (token, password/state, PAT revocation, session or MFA challenge) is in ONE WithTransaction; the two flagged writes are AddPasswordHistory+PrunePasswordHistory AFTER that commit, best-effort (besteffort.Run), exactly as ChangePassword/applyNewPassword and BootstrapSystem do. A lost history row only weakens the reuse check for this one password and never undoes or contradicts the committed consume; the next password change writes history again. #2693 review (2026-11-20): Also post-commit: the eviction of the account's other sessions (deleteSessionsForUserAndEvict), outside the transaction and invisible to this guard; its failure is audited loudly (EventSessionRevocationFailed), the same pattern as ChangePassword.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).BackfillPendingAuditEvents
column3: SUSPEND-AUDIT-LOUD: each owed row is claimed and appended in ONE transaction (appendOwedAudit); the other writes are RecordPendingAuditEventFailure bookkeeping (attempt count, last error) on a row that stays pending. Independent per row and self-healing: a failed note leaves the row pending for the next pass, and a row is never written twice (the claim is a DELETE in the append transaction).

column1: AUDIT:(*KeyorixCore).ReissueOneTimePassword
column3: AUDIT-TX-3: the reissue row is now written INSIDE the transaction (fail closed, withAuditedMutation) and AddPasswordHistory is a later post-commit best-effort write by design (ADR-025, self-healing on the next password change, same as CreateUser). The audit row therefore precedes only a write that is allowed to be lost, and the row is never the unaudited-change case this guard exists for. #2693 review (2026-11-20): Wording out of date: it is now a two-commit split (MERGE-FIX-3482G); commit 1 (restriction plus session end) is owed via runOwedAuditMutation, commit 2 (the credential) fails closed via commitSplitRemainder.

column1: (*KeyorixCore).resealAuditCheckpoint
column3: admin audit accept-loss (AUDIT-ACCEPT-LOSS-1), offline under the exclusive lock: CreateAuditCheckpoint then SetSystemMetadata (the high-water mark lowered to the sealed chain). A stop between them reads BROKEN (the old mark does not authenticate under the new seal binding) and a re-run of the command resumes (auditStateBehindSeals) and rewrites both from the sealed walk. Guard: TestAuditSeal_CrashAtEveryStepResumes.
